source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Existing public labels match all selected Hebrew records in Jeremiah 21–40. The final capture clause at 38:28 remains bound inside that verse; no relabeling performed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Identifies the two envoys and carries their speech into the next verse; this Pashhur has a different father from the man in chapter 20.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchijah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying,
verses.after: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD** when King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to him. They said,
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchijah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the request as a hopeful possibility, not a promise of rescue.
verses.before: “Please inquire of the LORD for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all his wonders, so that he will withdraw from us.”
verses.after: “Please inquire of the **LORD** for us. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war on us. Perhaps the **LORD** will act for us with all his wonders and make him withdraw.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Please inquire of the LORD for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all his wonders, so that he will withdraw from us.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the reply addressed through the messengers.
verses.before: Then Jeremiah said to them, “Thus you will say to Zedekiah:
verses.after: Jeremiah told them, “This is what you must say to Zedekiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeremiah said to them, “Thus you shall say to Zedekiah:

verses.rationale: Retains the weapon reversal and the ambiguous object of gathering rather than silently substituting one interpretation.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Look, I am turning back the weapons of war that are in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the wall, and I will gather them into the midst of this city.
verses.after: ‘The **LORD**, the God of Israel, says: I am turning back the weapons in your hands—the weapons you are using against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans besieging you outside the wall. I will gather them into the middle of this city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Look, I am turning back the weapons of war that are in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the wall, and I will gather them into the midst of this city.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic divine opponent and the repeated force of the anger terms.
verses.before: I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger and fury and great wrath.
verses.after: I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger, wrath, and great fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger and fury and great wrath.

verses.rationale: Keeps animals within the threatened destruction and identifies plague as the means.
verses.before: I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both human and animal. They will die by a great plague.
verses.after: I will strike down the inhabitants of this city, both people and animals. A terrible plague will kill them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both human and animal. They will die by a great plague.

verses.rationale: Keeps the survivors, the three disasters, and the king's uncompromising violence distinct.
verses.before: Afterward, says the LORD, I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, the people, and people who survive in this city from plague, sword, and famine into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of people who seek their lives. He will strike them with the edge of the sword. He will not spare them or have pity or compassion.”
verses.after: After that, declares the **LORD**, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, and the people—those left in this city after the plague, the sword, and the famine—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies, to those seeking their lives. He will put them to the sword without sparing them, without pity, without compassion.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward, says the LORD, I will give Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants, the people, and those who survive in this city from plague, sword, and famine into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their lives. He will strike them with the edge of the sword. He will not spare them or have pity or compassion.”

verses.rationale: Maintains the two ways as the framing image for the concrete choices that follow.
verses.before: “And to this people you will say: Thus says the LORD: Look, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.
verses.after: “Tell this people: ‘The **LORD** says: Look, I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And to this people you shall say: Thus says the LORD: Look, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form for living and retains life as plunder, an image of survival with nothing else secured.
verses.before: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword, famine, or plague; but whoever goes out and falls away to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live, and their life will be to them as plunder.
verses.after: Anyone who stays in this city will die by sword, famine, or plague. Anyone who goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans besieging you will live; that person's own life will be their plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever remains in this city will die by sword, famine, or plague; but whoever goes out and falls away to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live, and their life will be to them as plunder.

verses.rationale: Preserves the face image and the contrast between harm and good without turning disaster into a moral label.
verses.before: For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, says the LORD. It will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
verses.after: For I have set my face against this city for harm, not for good, declares the **LORD**. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, says the LORD. It shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

verses.rationale: Marks the shift to the royal household without inventing a new named king.
verses.before: “And concerning the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD, house of David.
verses.after: “To the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the **LORD**!
verses.tsw_comparator: “And concerning the house of the king of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD, house of David.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form 'your deeds'; retains morning justice, rescue, and unquenchable fire in verse-contained poetry.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Execute justice in the morning, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor, lest my fury go out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your deeds.
verses.after: House of David, the **LORD** says: Administer justice each morning. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the oppressor's hand, or my fury will break out like fire and burn with no one to put it out because of your evil deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Execute justice in the morning, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor, lest my fury go out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it because of the evil of your deeds.

verses.rationale: Makes the city's confident voice audible while preserving the unusual valley and plateau imagery.
verses.before: Look, I am against you, inhabitant of the valley, rock of the plain, says the LORD, you who say, ‘Who can come down against us? Who can enter our dwellings?’
verses.after: I am against you, you who live in the valley, on the rock of the plateau, declares the **LORD**— you who say, ‘Who can come down against us? Who can enter our homes?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am against you, inhabitant of the valley, rock of the plain, says the LORD, you who say, ‘Who can come down against us? Who can enter our dwellings?’

verses.rationale: Retains the fruit metaphor and the shift to the city's forest rather than explaining the image within the oracle.
verses.before: I will attend to you according to the fruit of your deeds, says the LORD. I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume all that is around her.”
verses.after: I will call you to account for the fruit of your deeds, declares the **LORD**. I will set fire to her forest, and it will consume everything around her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will attend to you according to the fruit of your deeds, says the LORD. I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume all that is around her.”

verses.rationale: Places the oracle at the palace and preserves the command to go down.
verses.before: Thus said the LORD: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there,
verses.after: The **LORD** said, “Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and speak this word there:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus said the LORD: “Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there,

verses.rationale: Keeps the king and the wider palace audience together.
verses.before: and say, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah who sits on the throne of David—you, your servants, and your people who enter through these gates.
verses.after: ‘Hear the word of the **LORD**, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne—you, your servants, and your people who enter these gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: and say, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah who sits on the throne of David—you, your servants, and your people who enter through these gates.

verses.rationale: Names the vulnerable groups and retains both mistreatment and killing as concrete prohibitions.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Practice justice and righteousness. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not wrong or do violence to the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
verses.after: The **LORD** says: Do what is just and right. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the oppressor's hand. Do not wrong or mistreat the resident foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. Do not shed innocent blood in this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Practice justice and righteousness. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not wrong or do violence to the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic condition and follows the read form for the king's servants.
verses.before: For if you truly do this thing, then kings who sit for David on his throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their servants and their people.
verses.after: If you truly carry out this word, kings who sit on David's throne will enter the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, each with his servants and his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if you truly do this thing, then kings who sit for David on his throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their servants and their people.

verses.rationale: Retains the oath by the speaker's own self and its conditional warning.
verses.before: But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by myself, says the LORD, that this house will become a desolation.’”
verses.after: But if you will not listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the **LORD**, this palace will become a ruin.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by myself, says the LORD, that this house shall become a desolation.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps both valued mountain regions and the sharp reversal into desolation.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon, yet surely I will make you a wilderness, cities without inhabitants.
verses.after: “For this is what the **LORD** says about the palace of the king of Judah: Though you are Gilead to me, the summit of Lebanon, I will make you a wilderness, a place of uninhabited towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon, yet surely I will make you a wilderness, cities without inhabitants.

verses.rationale: Preserves the setting apart of destroyers and the cedar image without softening the destruction.
verses.before: I will consecrate destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.
verses.after: I will set apart destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your finest cedars and throw them into the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will consecrate destroyers against you, each with his weapons. They will cut down your choice cedars and throw them into the fire.

verses.rationale: Lets foreign observers pose the question rather than adding narrator commentary.
verses.before: Many nations will pass by this city, and each will say to his neighbor, ‘Why has the LORD done this to this great city?’
verses.after: “Many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, ‘Why did the **LORD** do this to this great city?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Many nations will pass by this city, and each will say to his neighbor, ‘Why has the LORD done this to this great city?’

verses.rationale: Retains covenant, worship, and service as the stated explanation.
verses.before: And they will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them.’”
verses.after: They will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the **LORD** their God, bowed down to other gods, and served them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And they will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them.’”

verses.rationale: Clarifies the royal setting while keeping the contrast between death and irreversible exile.
verses.before: Do not weep for the dead, and do not mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he will return no more or see the land of his birth.
verses.after: Do not weep for the dead king or mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who is leaving, for he will never return or see the land of his birth again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not weep for the dead, and do not mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he will return no more or see the land of his birth.

verses.rationale: Preserves Shallum's name and succession rather than replacing his name with a harmonized alternative.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of Josiah his father and who went out from this place: “He will not return here again.
verses.after: For the **LORD** says this about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who became king in place of his father Josiah and left this place: “He will never return here.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of Josiah his father and who went out from this place: “He will not return here again.

verses.rationale: Keeps death in exile and the repeated denial of return.
verses.before: But in the place where they carried him into exile, there he will die, and he will see this land no more.”
verses.after: He will die in the place where they have exiled him. He will never see this land again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But in the place where they carried him into exile, there he will die, and he will see this land no more.”

verses.rationale: Makes unpaid labor explicit and preserves the paired construction imagery.
verses.before: Woe to the one who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor serve for nothing and does not give him his wages,
verses.after: Woe to the man who builds his house through injustice and his upper rooms through wrongdoing, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and never pays him his wages!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the one who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor serve for nothing and does not give him his wages,

verses.rationale: Retains the first-person building ambition and the specific expensive materials and color.
verses.before: who says, “I will build myself a large house with spacious upper rooms,” and cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it with red.
verses.after: He says, “I will build myself a spacious house with airy upper rooms.” He cuts windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it vermilion.
verses.tsw_comparator: who says, “I will build myself a large house with spacious upper rooms,” and cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it with red.

verses.rationale: Renders the cedar competition as a question and retains the father's ordinary enjoyment alongside justice.
verses.before: Do you reign because you compete in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and practice justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.
verses.after: Does competing in cedar make you a king? Did not your father eat and drink and do what was just and right? Then things went well for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you reign because you compete in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink and practice justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.

verses.rationale: Connects knowing the speaker to defending the vulnerable without adding a doctrinal definition.
verses.before: He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. Is this not to know me? says the LORD.
verses.after: He defended the cause of the poor and needy; then things went well. Is that not what it means to know me? declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it was well. Is this not to know me? says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the accusation's focus on gain, bloodshed, and oppressive action.
verses.before: But your eyes and your heart are only for your unjust gain, for shedding innocent blood, and for oppression and violence.
verses.after: But your eyes and your heart are set only on your dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood, and on practicing oppression and violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: But your eyes and your heart are only for your unjust gain, for shedding innocent blood, and for oppression and violence.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four lament formulas and names the king precisely.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: “They will not lament for him, ‘Alas, my brother!’ or ‘Alas, sister!’ They will not lament for him, ‘Alas, lord!’ or ‘Alas, his majesty!’
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD** says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They will not mourn for him, “Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!” They will not mourn for him, “Alas, my lord! Alas, his splendor!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: “They will not lament for him, ‘Alas, my brother!’ or ‘Alas, sister!’ They will not lament for him, ‘Alas, lord!’ or ‘Alas, his majesty!’

verses.rationale: Retains the degrading animal comparison and disposal of the body.
verses.before: He will be buried with the burial of a donkey, dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.after: He will have a donkey's burial— dragged away and thrown beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will be buried with the burial of a donkey, dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three locations and the lovers image without replacing it with an explanatory political label.
verses.before: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan. Cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers are broken.
verses.after: Climb Lebanon and cry out! Raise your voice in Bashan! Cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers have been crushed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan. Cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers are broken.

verses.rationale: Keeps the refusal as direct speech and the repeated listening motif.
verses.before: I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way from your youth: you have not listened to my voice.
verses.after: I spoke to you when you were secure, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way from your youth: you have never listened to my voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, “I will not listen.” This has been your way from your youth: you have not listened to my voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Hebrew shepherding wordplay and separates captivity from shame.
verses.before: The wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then surely you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your evil.
verses.after: The wind will shepherd all your shepherds away, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then surely you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your evil.

verses.rationale: Uses a pity reading of the difficult verb and records its uncertainty in a note; preserves nesting and labor pain.
verses.before: You who dwell in Lebanon, nested among the cedars, how you will groan when pains come upon you, anguish like one giving birth!
verses.after: You who live in Lebanon, who nest among the cedars, how you will be pitied when pangs come upon you, pain like that of a woman giving birth!
verses.tsw_comparator: You who dwell in Lebanon, nested among the cedars, how you will groan when pains come upon you, anguish like one giving birth!

verses.rationale: Maintains the oath and intimate signet image while making the turn to direct address readable.
verses.before: “As I live,” says the LORD, “even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, even from there I would tear you off.
verses.after: “As I live, declares the **LORD**, even if you, Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would pull you off.
verses.tsw_comparator: “As I live,” says the LORD, “even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, even from there I would tear you off.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named recipients and the king's fear.
verses.before: I will give you into the hand of people who seek your life, into the hand of those whom you fear, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
verses.after: I will hand you over to those seeking your life, to those you fear—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you into the hand of those who seek your life, into the hand of those whom you fear, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of the Chaldeans.

verses.rationale: Keeps the mother's shared exile and the contrast between birthplace and place of death.
verses.before: I will hurl you and your mother who bore you into another land where you were not born, and there you will die.
verses.after: I will hurl you and the mother who gave birth to you into another country, where neither of you was born. There you will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will hurl you and your mother who bore you into another land where you were not born, and there you will die.

verses.rationale: Retains the shift to third person and the repeated return language.
verses.before: But to the land to which they lift up their life to return, there they will not return.”
verses.after: They will never return to the land they long to return to.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the land to which they lift up their life to return, there they will not return.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the rhetorical questions, offspring, and discarded vessel image.
verses.before: Is this man Coniah a despised, shattered vessel, a vessel no one desires? Why are he and his offspring hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?
verses.after: Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot, a vessel no one wants? Why have he and his offspring been hurled away, thrown into a land they do not know?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this man Coniah a despised, shattered vessel, a vessel no one desires? Why are he and his offspring hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold summons instead of reducing its urgency.
verses.before: Land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
verses.after: Land, land, land! Hear the word of the **LORD**!
verses.tsw_comparator: Land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!

verses.rationale: Keeps 'childless' alongside the explicit dynastic explanation, without denying the offspring already mentioned.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Write this man down as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days, for none of his offspring will prosper sitting on the throne of David and ruling again in Judah.”
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “Record this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime. For none of his offspring will prosper by sitting on David's throne and ruling again in Judah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Write this man down as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days, for none of his offspring will prosper sitting on the throne of David and ruling again in Judah.”

verses.rationale: Retains the shepherd accusation and the flock's belonging to the speaker.
verses.before: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says the LORD.
verses.after: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture!” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated attending verb as a reversal from failed care to accountability.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who shepherd my people: “You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and you have not attended to them. Look, I am attending to you for the evil of your deeds,” says the LORD.
verses.after: So this is what the **LORD**, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who tend my people: “You have scattered my flock and driven them away. You have not attended to them. Now I will attend to you for your evil deeds, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who shepherd my people: “You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and you have not attended to them. Look, I am attending to you for the evil of your deeds,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine responsibility for dispersal and the fruitful-and-multiply language.
verses.before: “Then I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I drove them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
verses.after: I myself will gather what remains of my flock from all the countries where I drove them. I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I drove them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.

verses.rationale: Retains future care, freedom from fear, and the assurance that none are missing.
verses.before: I will raise up shepherds over them who will shepherd them. They will no longer fear or be terrified, and none will be missing,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will appoint shepherds over them who will tend them. They will no longer be afraid or dismayed, and none will be missing, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will raise up shepherds over them who will shepherd them. They will no longer fear or be terrified, and none will be missing,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the growth image and the king's wisdom and justice without identifying a later individual in the translation.
verses.before: “Look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will reign as king and act wisely and practice justice and righteousness in the land.
verses.after: “Look, days are coming, declares the **LORD**, when I will raise up a righteous Branch for David. A king will reign and act wisely, doing what is just and right in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will reign as king and act wisely and practice justice and righteousness in the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves both kingdoms and the royal name while leaving its theological implications to interpretation.
verses.before: In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: ‘The LORD Is Our Righteousness.’
verses.after: In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live securely. This is the name by which he will be called: ‘The **LORD** is our righteousness.’
verses.tsw_comparator: In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: ‘The LORD Is Our Righteousness.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the old oath formula as the first half of the contrast.

verses.rationale: Marks the prophetic heading and preserves physical distress and drunkenness as comparisons.

verses.after: Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me; all my bones shake. I have become like a drunk, like a man overcome by wine, because of the **LORD** and because of his holy words.

verses.rationale: Keeps the curse, mourning land, and misuse of strength without making the imagery merely psychological.

verses.after: For the land is full of adulterers. Because of the curse the land mourns, and the wilderness pastures have dried up. Their course is evil, and their strength serves what is wrong.

verses.rationale: Retains the indictment of both offices and wrongdoing in the divine house.

verses.tsw_comparator: “For both prophet and priest are profane; even in my house I have found their evil,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps darkness, slipping, and falling together and renders visitation as accountability.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the Samaria charge from the Jerusalem accusation that follows.
verses.before: “Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something offensive: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.
verses.after: “Among the prophets of Samaria I saw a repulsive thing: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something offensive: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

verses.rationale: Preserves the strengthening-hands image and the separate comparisons with Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.before: But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrifying: committing adultery and walking in falsehood. They strengthen the hands of evildoers so that no one turns from evil. All of them have become to me like Sodom, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.
verses.after: But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrifying thing: adultery and a life of lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so no one turns back from wickedness. To me they have all become like Sodom, and the city's inhabitants like Gomorrah.”

verses.rationale: Retains wormwood and poisoned water as bitter consequences rather than substituting abstract punishment.

verses.after: So the **LORD** of hosts says this about the prophets: “Look, I will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, for godlessness has spread from the prophets of Jerusalem throughout the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts concerning the prophets: Look, I will feed them wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem profaneness has gone out into all the land.”

verses.rationale: Makes the effect of empty prophecy readable while preserving heart and mouth as contrasting sources.

verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts says: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They fill you with empty hopes. They speak visions from their own hearts, not from the mouth of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They make you empty; they speak a vision from their own heart, not from the mouth of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both audiences and distinguishes the two false assurances.
verses.before: They continually say to people who despise me, ‘The LORD has spoken: You will have peace.’ And to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his heart they say, ‘No disaster will come upon you.’
verses.after: They keep telling those who despise me, ‘The **LORD** has said: You will have peace.’ To everyone who follows a stubborn heart they say, ‘No disaster will come upon you.’

verses.rationale: Follows the read form 'his word' and preserves the challenge about access to the divine council.

verses.after: But who has stood in the council of the **LORD** to see and hear his word? Who has paid attention to his word and listened?

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated storm movement and its target.

verses.after: Look! The storm of the **LORD**! Wrath has burst out, a whirling storm; it whirls down on the heads of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Retains completion of the heart's purposes and future understanding without imposing an end-times timetable.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and established the purposes of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it clearly.
verses.after: The anger of the **LORD** will not turn back until he has done and accomplished what his heart intends. In days to come you will understand it clearly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and established the purposes of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it clearly.

verses.rationale: Preserves the balanced denials and unauthorized activity.

verses.after: I did not send these prophets, but they ran. I did not speak to them, but they prophesied.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing and turning as the effects the false prophets failed to produce.

verses.after: If they had stood in my council, they would have made my people hear my words and turned them back from their evil way and from their evil deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they had stood in my council, they would have caused my people to hear my words and turned them from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Preserves the question's spatial contrast without reducing it to a slogan about omnipresence.

verses.after: Am I a God only nearby, declares the **LORD**, and not a God far away?
verses.tsw_comparator: Am I a God nearby,” says the LORD, “and not a God far away?

verses.rationale: Keeps both questions and both repeated declarations.
verses.before: Can anyone hide in secret places so that I do not see them?” says the LORD. “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” says the LORD.
verses.after: Can anyone hide in secret places where I cannot see them? declares the **LORD**. Do I not fill heaven and earth? declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Can anyone hide in secret places so that I do not see them?” says the LORD. “Do I not fill heaven and earth?” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated dream claim and the misuse of the speaker's name.

verses.rationale: Gives the elliptical question readable English while retaining the repeated heart and lying-prophecy language.

verses.rationale: Preserves forgetting the name and the comparison with ancestral Baal worship.

verses.rationale: Keeps the limited permission to report a dream and the agricultural distinction from faithful speech.

verses.after: Let the prophet who has a dream tell the dream. But let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain? declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The prophet who has a dream, let him tell the dream; but the one who has my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain?” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both forceful images and the rhetorical question.
verses.before: “Is not my word like fire,” says the LORD, “and like a hammer that shatters rock?
verses.after: Is not my word like fire, declares the **LORD**, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Is not my word like fire,” says the LORD, “and like a hammer that shatters rock?

verses.rationale: Keeps the first 'I am against' accusation and the theft of words.

verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore look, I am against the prophets,” says the LORD, “who steal my words from one another.

verses.rationale: Preserves the claim to an oracle without inserting an additional divine name into the quoted formula.

verses.after: I am against the prophets, declares the **LORD**, who use their tongues to pronounce oracles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am against the prophets,” says the LORD, “who use their tongues and declare, ‘He says.’

verses.rationale: Retains both denials of authorization and the emphatic absence of benefit.
verses.before: Look, I am against people who prophesy false dreams,” says the LORD, “and tell them and lead my people astray by their falsehoods and reckless boasting. Yet I did not send them or command them, and they do not profit this people at all,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I am against those who prophesy false dreams, declares the **LORD**. They tell them and lead my people astray with their lies and their reckless boasting. I did not send them or commission them. They bring this people no benefit at all, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am against those who prophesy false dreams,” says the LORD, “and tell them and lead my people astray by their falsehoods and reckless boasting. Yet I did not send them or command them, and they do not profit this people at all,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned word division 'What burden?' and keeps burden as the oracle word needed for the following wordplay.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prohibition's three groups and household consequence.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two acceptable questions and the brother wording rather than broadening every relationship.

verses.rationale: Retains the burden reversal and the full identification of the living God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated questions now directed to a prophet.
verses.before: Thus you will say to the prophet: ‘What has the LORD answered you?’ or ‘What has the LORD spoken?’

verses.rationale: Preserves all repetitions of the prohibited formula and leaves the sentence open for its consequence.

verses.rationale: Follows the pointed forgetting verb while flagging the difficult accompanying form and alternative burden wordplay in a note.

verses.rationale: Preserves the historical setting, royal names, and distinct skilled workers.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated degree of goodness and badness and the first-ripe comparison.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full repeated report rather than shortening the vision's exchange.

verses.rationale: Preserves the eye image and the paired building and planting verbs linking the book's promises.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unfavorable comparison and both locations of the remaining people.

verses.rationale: Retains the accumulating terms of public disgrace and the speaker's agency in dispersal.

verses.after: Do not follow other gods to serve them and bow down to them. Do not provoke me with what your hands have made, and I will not bring harm on you.’

verses.before: But you did not listen to me,” says the LORD, “so that you provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.”
verses.after: ‘But you did not listen to me, declares the **LORD**. You provoked me with what your hands made, bringing harm on yourselves.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But you did not listen to me,” says the LORD, “so that you provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.”

verses.rationale: Leaves the causal sentence open for the announced action.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Because you have not listened to my words,
verses.after: “So the **LORD** of hosts says: ‘Because you have not listened to my words,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Because you have not listened to my words,

verses.rationale: Keeps the surprising servant title, the wider nations, and the force of devoted destruction.
verses.before: look, I am sending and taking all the clans of the north,” says the LORD, “and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land, against its inhabitants, and against all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them a horror, a hissing, and everlasting ruins.
verses.after: I will send for all the clans of the north, declares the **LORD**, and for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them a horror, something to hiss at, and lasting ruins.
verses.tsw_comparator: look, I am sending and taking all the clans of the north,” says the LORD, “and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land, against its inhabitants, and against all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them a horror, a hissing, and everlasting ruins.

verses.rationale: Preserves the accumulation of celebration and ordinary household life extinguished.
verses.before: I will destroy from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, the sound of millstones and the light of the lamp.
verses.after: I will put an end among them to the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of bridegroom and bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will destroy from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, the sound of millstones and the light of the lamp.

verses.rationale: Retains the nations as subjects of the seventy-year service rather than narrowing the term to one exile.
verses.before: This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
verses.after: This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
verses.tsw_comparator: This whole land will become a ruin and a horror, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

verses.rationale: Keeps Babylon's later accountability and the completed seventy years.
verses.before: Then, when seventy years are completed, I will attend to the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt,” says the LORD, “and to the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it everlasting desolations.
verses.after: When seventy years are complete, I will call the king of Babylon, that nation, and the land of the Chaldeans to account for their guilt, declares the **LORD**. I will make it a lasting waste.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then, when seventy years are completed, I will attend to the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt,” says the LORD, “and to the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it everlasting desolations.

verses.rationale: Follows the read spelling of bringing and preserves the reference to the written scroll.
verses.before: I will bring upon that land all my words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
verses.after: I will bring upon that land all the words I have spoken against it, everything written in this scroll that Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring upon that land all my words that I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reversal of service into enslavement and the hand-work repayment motif.
verses.before: For many nations and great kings will make slaves even of them, and I will repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands.”
verses.after: For many nations and great kings will enslave them in turn. I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For many nations and great kings will make slaves even of them, and I will repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the cup as an enacted prophetic image and identifies its wine with wrath.
verses.before: For thus said the LORD, the God of Israel, to me: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD**, the God of Israel, said to me: “Take from my hand this cup of wine, the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus said the LORD, the God of Israel, to me: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.

verses.rationale: Retains the disturbing bodily effects and the sword as their cause.
verses.before: They will drink and stagger and act madly because of the sword that I am sending among them.”
verses.after: They will drink, stagger, and go mad because of the sword I am sending among them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They will drink and stagger and act madly because of the sword that I am sending among them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine-name occurrences and introduces the complete list.
verses.before: So I took the cup from the hand of the LORD and made all the nations to whom the LORD sent me drink:
verses.after: So I took the cup from the hand of the **LORD** and made all the nations to whom the **LORD** sent me drink it:
verses.tsw_comparator: So I took the cup from the hand of the LORD and made all the nations to whom the LORD sent me drink:

verses.rationale: Keeps the list's first recipients and the text's retrospective 'today'.
verses.before: Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, a hissing, and a curse, as they are this day;
verses.after: Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and officials—to make them a ruin, a horror, something to hiss at, and a curse, as they are today;
verses.tsw_comparator: Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, a hissing, and a curse, as they are this day;

verses.rationale: Preserves every tier of the Egyptian audience.
verses.before: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;
verses.after: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;

verses.rationale: Retains the mixed population and every named Philistine place, including Ashdod's remnant.
verses.before: all the mixed people; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
verses.after: all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what remains of Ashdod;
verses.tsw_comparator: all the mixed people; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;

verses.rationale: Keeps the three neighboring peoples without expanding the list.
verses.before: Edom, Moab, and the children of Ammon;
verses.after: Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites;
verses.tsw_comparator: Edom, Moab, and the children of Ammon;

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated 'all' and the maritime extension.
verses.before: all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastland beyond the sea;
verses.after: all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
verses.tsw_comparator: all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastland beyond the sea;

verses.rationale: Keeps the three names and the distinctive hair practice rather than replacing it with a guessed ethnic label.
verses.before: Dedan, Tema, Buz, and everyone who clip the corners of their hair;
verses.after: Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the edges of their hair;
verses.tsw_comparator: Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who clip the corners of their hair;

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Arabia from the mixed desert peoples, preserving the similar-sounding Hebrew terms.
verses.before: all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed people who dwell in the wilderness;
verses.after: all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples living in the wilderness;
verses.tsw_comparator: all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed people who dwell in the wilderness;

verses.rationale: Retains Zimri despite uncertain identification and preserves the three royal groups.
verses.before: all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
verses.after: all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
verses.tsw_comparator: all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;

verses.rationale: Keeps the widening geographical scope and the encoded final name rather than replacing it silently with Babylon.
verses.before: all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the kingdoms of the earth that are on the face of the ground. And the king of Sheshach will drink after them.
verses.after: all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another; and all the kingdoms on the face of the earth. After them the king of Sheshach will drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the kingdoms of the earth that are on the face of the ground. And the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sequence of humiliating physical commands and its violent cause.
verses.before: “Then you will say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Drink, become drunk, vomit, fall, and rise no more because of the sword that I am sending among you.
verses.after: “Tell them: ‘The **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, vomit, fall, and never rise again, because of the sword I am sending among you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then you shall say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Drink, become drunk, vomit, fall, and rise no more because of the sword that I am sending among you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the refusal hypothetical and the response emphatic.
verses.before: And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you will say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: You will surely drink!
verses.after: If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, tell them: ‘The **LORD** of hosts says: You will certainly drink!
verses.tsw_comparator: And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, then you shall say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: You shall surely drink!

verses.rationale: Retains the name-bearing city and the repeated denial of exemption.
verses.before: For look, I am beginning to bring harm upon the city that is called by my name, and should you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am calling for a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: For look, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my name. Do you expect to go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning a sword against everyone who lives on the earth, declares the **LORD** of hosts.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am beginning to bring harm upon the city that is called by my name, and should you go entirely unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, for I am calling for a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves the roaring, dwelling, pasture, and wine-treading images in their sequence.
verses.before: “And you, prophesy against them all these words and say to them: The LORD will roar from on high and from his holy dwelling give his voice. He will roar mightily against his pasture; he will shout like people who tread grapes against all the inhabitants of the earth.
verses.after: “You must prophesy all these words to them. Tell them: The **LORD** roars from on high; from his holy dwelling he raises his voice. He roars mightily over his pasture. Like those treading grapes, he shouts against all the inhabitants of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, prophesy against them all these words and say to them: The LORD will roar from on high and from his holy dwelling give his voice. He will roar mightily against his pasture; he will shout like those who tread grapes against all the inhabitants of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the legal dispute, all-flesh scope, and sentence against the wicked.
verses.before: The tumult will reach to the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a controversy with the nations. He enters into judgment with all flesh; the wicked he gives to the sword,” says the LORD.
verses.after: The uproar reaches the ends of the earth, for the **LORD** has a case against the nations. He brings all flesh to judgment; he hands the wicked over to the sword, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tumult will reach to the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a controversy with the nations. He enters into judgment with all flesh; the wicked he gives to the sword,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves movement across nations and the storm's remote origin.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, disaster is going out from nation to nation, and a great storm is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts says: Look! Disaster spreads from nation to nation; a mighty storm rises from the farthest reaches of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, disaster is going out from nation to nation, and a great storm is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains all three denied burial acts and the deliberately degrading comparison.
verses.before: Those slain by the LORD on that day will be from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. They will not be lamented, gathered, or buried. They will become manure on the face of the ground.
verses.after: “On that day, those slain by the **LORD** will lie from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned, gathered, or buried. They will be dung on the surface of the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those slain by the LORD on that day will be from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. They will not be lamented, gathered, or buried. They will become manure on the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult scattering phrase and the falling-vessel comparison, with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Wail, shepherds, and cry out! Roll yourselves in ashes, leaders of the flock! For your days for slaughter are fulfilled, and I will scatter you, and you will fall like a precious vessel.
verses.after: Wail and cry out, shepherds! Roll in the dust, leaders of the flock! Your days for slaughter and scattering have come; you will fall like a precious vessel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wail, shepherds, and cry out! Roll yourselves in ashes, leaders of the flock! For your days for slaughter are fulfilled, and I will scatter you, and you will fall like a precious vessel.

verses.rationale: Preserves both parallel denials of refuge.
verses.before: Flight will perish from the shepherds, and escape from the leaders of the flock.
verses.after: The shepherds will have nowhere to flee; the leaders of the flock will have no escape.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flight will perish from the shepherds, and escape from the leaders of the flock.

verses.rationale: Makes the sound construction natural while preserving the cause of the lament.
verses.before: A sound—the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock! For the LORD is devastating their pasture.
verses.after: Listen to the shepherds' cry, the wailing of the leaders of the flock! The **LORD** is devastating their pasture.
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound—the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock! For the LORD is devastating their pasture.

verses.rationale: Keeps silence in places formerly at peace and the burning-anger image.
verses.before: The peaceful pastures are silenced because of the burning anger of the LORD.
verses.after: The peaceful pastures lie silent because of the **LORD**'s burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: The peaceful pastures are silenced because of the burning anger of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the lion's departure and the pointed source's oppressor reading, flagged in a note.
verses.before: Like a young lion he has left his thicket, for their land has become a horror because of the fierce oppressor and because of his burning anger.
verses.after: Like a young lion he has left his lair. Their land has become a horror because of the fury of the oppressor and because of his burning anger.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a young lion he has left his thicket, for their land has become a horror because of the fierce oppressor and because of his burning anger.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reign's beginning without assigning an unstated year.
verses.before: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD, saying,
verses.after: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the **LORD**:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD, saying,

verses.rationale: Clarifies towns as their visiting inhabitants and retains the three divine-name occurrences and completeness command.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD: Stand in the court of the house of the LORD and speak to all the cities of Judah who come to worship in the house of the LORD all the words that I command you to speak to them. Do not hold back a word.
verses.after: “The **LORD** says: Stand in the courtyard of the house of the **LORD**. Speak to the people of all Judah's towns who come to worship at the house of the **LORD**. Tell them everything I command you to say. Do not leave out a word.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD: Stand in the court of the house of the LORD and speak to all the cities of Judah who come to worship in the house of the LORD all the words that I command you to speak to them. Do not hold back a word.

verses.rationale: Preserves the possibility, individual response, and conditional relenting.
verses.before: Perhaps they will listen and turn, each from his evil way, so that I may relent concerning the harm that I intend to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.
verses.after: Perhaps they will listen and turn back, each from their evil way. Then I will relent from the disaster I intend to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Perhaps they will listen and turn, each from his evil way, so that I may relent concerning the harm that I intend to do to them because of the evil of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Renders torah as instruction while retaining its authoritative placement before the audience.
verses.before: You will say to them: Thus says the LORD: If you will not listen to me, to walk in my instruction that I have set before you,
verses.after: Tell them: ‘The **LORD** says: If you will not listen to me and follow the instruction I have set before you,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall say to them: Thus says the LORD: If you will not listen to me, to walk in my instruction that I have set before you,

verses.rationale: Keeps persistent sending and the interrupting reminder of refusal.
verses.before: to listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I send to you, rising early and sending them, though you have not listened,
verses.after: or listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I keep sending to you again and again—though you have not listened—
verses.tsw_comparator: to listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I send to you, rising early and sending them, though you have not listened,

verses.rationale: Retains Shiloh as a named warning and follows the read demonstrative without extra implication.
verses.before: then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.”
verses.after: then I will make this house like Shiloh and make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the three groups who heard the warning.
verses.before: The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the seizure and emphatic death demand without attributing it only to the priests.
verses.before: When Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him, saying, “You will surely die!
verses.after: When Jeremiah finished saying everything the **LORD** had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him. “You must die!” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him, saying, “You shall surely die!

verses.rationale: Retains the disputed prophecy and the surrounding crowd.
verses.before: Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘This house will become like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate, without inhabitant’?” And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: “Why have you prophesied in the name of the **LORD** that this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be ruined and uninhabited?” All the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘This house will become like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate, without inhabitant’?” And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the move upward and identifies the gate setting for the hearing.
verses.before: When the officials of Judah heard these things, they went up from the king’s house to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.
verses.after: When Judah's officials heard about this, they came up from the royal palace to the house of the **LORD** and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the **LORD**'s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the officials of Judah heard these things, they went up from the king’s house to the house of the LORD and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD’s house.

verses.rationale: Makes the legal demand explicit and retains the appeal to the audience's own hearing.
verses.before: Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the officials and to all the people, saying, “A sentence of death belongs to this man, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears.”
verses.after: The priests and prophets said to the officials and all the people, “This man deserves a death sentence! He has prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the officials and to all the people, saying, “A sentence of death belongs to this man, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears.”

verses.rationale: Preserves his defense as a claim of divine commissioning.
verses.before: Jeremiah spoke to all the officials and to all the people, saying, “The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.
verses.after: Jeremiah answered all the officials and all the people: “The **LORD** sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the words you have heard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah spoke to all the officials and to all the people, saying, “The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words that you have heard.

verses.rationale: Keeps both conduct and deeds and the conditional possibility of relenting.
verses.before: Now therefore make your ways and your deeds good, and listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and the LORD will relent concerning the harm that he has spoken against you.
verses.after: Now put your ways and your deeds right. Listen to the voice of the **LORD** your God, and the **LORD** will relent from the disaster he has announced against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore make your ways and your deeds good, and listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and the LORD will relent concerning the harm that he has spoken against you.

verses.rationale: Retains surrender to their power without endorsing their judgment as actually just.
verses.before: But as for me, look, I am in your hand. Do with me as is good and right in your eyes.
verses.after: As for me, here I am in your hands. Do to me whatever seems good and right to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, look, I am in your hand. Do with me as is good and right in your eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic warning of bloodguilt and the asserted truth of the commission.
verses.before: Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its inhabitants, for in truth the LORD sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears.”
verses.after: But know this for certain: if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, this city, and its inhabitants. For the **LORD** truly sent me to speak all these words in your hearing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon its inhabitants, for in truth the LORD sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the people's changed alignment and the reversal of the death verdict.
verses.before: Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, “There is no sentence of death for this man, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.”
verses.after: Then the officials and all the people told the priests and prophets, “This man does not deserve a death sentence. He has spoken to us in the name of the **LORD** our God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, “There is no sentence of death for this man, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.”

verses.rationale: Identifies the new speakers as some elders rather than every elder.
verses.before: Some of the elders of the land rose and spoke to all the assembly of the people, saying,
verses.after: Some of the elders of the land stood up and addressed the whole assembly of the people:
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of the elders of the land rose and spoke to all the assembly of the people, saying,

verses.rationale: Follows the read name Micah and preserves the quoted three-part devastation prophecy inside the verse paragraph.
verses.before: “Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and spoke to all the people of Judah, saying: ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.’
verses.after: “Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, ‘The **LORD** of hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field; Jerusalem will become heaps of rubble, and the temple hill a wooded height.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and spoke to all the people of Judah, saying: ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.’

verses.rationale: Retains the questions, three divine names, and the elders' warning about their own danger.
verses.before: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek the favor of the LORD, and did the LORD not relent concerning the harm he had spoken against them? But we are about to bring great harm upon ourselves.”
verses.after: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the **LORD** and seek the favor of the **LORD**, so that the **LORD** relented from the disaster he had announced against them? We are about to bring great harm on ourselves!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek the favor of the LORD, and did the LORD not relent concerning the harm he had spoken against them? But we are about to bring great harm upon ourselves.”

verses.rationale: Introduces the contrasting prophet without automatically making this an extension of the elders' speech.
verses.before: There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the LORD, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-Jearim. He prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah.
verses.after: There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the **LORD**: Uriah son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in words like Jeremiah's.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the LORD, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-Jearim. He prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king's pursuit, the prophet's fear, and the destination.
