verses.rationale: Uses the same rendering for all three occurrences of shalom to make the shared welfare connection audible.
verses.before: And seek the welfare of the city to which I have exiled you, and pray for it to the LORD, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.
verses.after: Seek the well-being of the city where I have exiled you, and pray to the **LORD** on its behalf. Its well-being will be your well-being.
verses.tsw_comparator: And seek the welfare of the city to which I have exiled you, and pray for it to the LORD, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.

verses.rationale: Preserves the causative dream wording, with the possible direct dreaming sense noted.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let the prophets among you, or your diviners, deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you cause to be dreamed.
verses.after: For the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let the prophets and diviners among you deceive you. Do not listen to the dreams you encourage them to dream.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let the prophets among you, or your diviners, deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you cause to be dreamed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the false use of the name and denial of commission.
verses.before: For they prophesy a lie to you in my name; I did not send them, declares the LORD.
verses.after: They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they prophesy a lie to you in my name; I did not send them, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains 'for Babylon' rather than converting it into seventy years for each exile.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will visit you and confirm to you my good word, to bring you back to this place.
verses.after: “For the **LORD** says: When seventy years are complete for Babylon, I will attend to you and fulfill my good promise to bring you back to this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will visit you and confirm to you my good word, to bring you back to this place.

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural exiled audience in context and preserves both future and hope without promising individual wealth.
verses.before: For I myself know the plans I am planning concerning you, declares the LORD—plans for well-being and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.
verses.after: For I know the plans I have for you, declares the **LORD**—plans for well-being, not for harm, to give you a future and hope.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I myself know the plans I am planning concerning you, declares the LORD—plans for well-being and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.

verses.rationale: Preserves calling, coming, praying, and the answer of listening.
verses.before: Then you will call upon me, and you will come and pray to me, and I will hear you.
verses.after: Then you will call on me, come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will call upon me, and you will come and pray to me, and I will hear you.

verses.rationale: Retains the connection between finding and whole-hearted seeking.
verses.before: You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
verses.after: You will seek me and find me when you search for me with your whole heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form for fortunes; keeps both declarations and the gathering from all places.
verses.before: I will be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes; I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I exiled you.
verses.after: I will let you find me, declares the **LORD**. I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and all the places where I drove you, declares the **LORD**. I will bring you back to the place from which I exiled you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes; I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I exiled you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exiles' claim as quoted speech leading into the response.
verses.before: Because you have said, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon"—
verses.after: “You have said, ‘The **LORD** has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you have said, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon"—

verses.rationale: Preserves the change of subject to those still in Jerusalem and the brother relationship.
verses.before: thus says the LORD concerning the king who sits on the throne of David, and concerning all the people who dwell in this city, your kindred who did not go out with you into exile,
verses.after: But this is what the **LORD** says about the king who sits on David's throne and all the people living in this city, your brothers who did not go into exile with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: thus says the LORD concerning the king who sits on the throne of David, and concerning all the people who dwell in this city, your kindred who did not go out with you into exile,

verses.rationale: Retains the three disasters and the repeated fig image connecting chapter 24.
verses.before: thus says the LORD of Hosts: I am sending against them sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them like rotten figs that cannot be eaten, so bad are they.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts says: I am sending sword, famine, and plague against them. I will make them like rotten figs, so bad they cannot be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: thus says the LORD of Hosts: I am sending against them sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them like rotten figs that cannot be eaten, so bad are they.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated disasters and all the public-disgrace terms, following the read horror form.
verses.before: I will pursue them with sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and a desolation, a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,
verses.after: I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague. I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth—a curse, a desolation, something to hiss at, and a reproach among all the nations where I drive them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will pursue them with sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, a curse and a desolation, a hissing and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them,

verses.rationale: Keeps the consequential shift from 'they' to 'you' rather than harmonizing the audience.
verses.before: because they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, when I sent to them my servants the prophets, sending them again and again. But you would not listen, declares the LORD.
verses.after: They did not listen to my words, declares the **LORD**, though I sent my servants the prophets to them again and again. And you did not listen either, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: because they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, when I sent to them my servants the prophets, sending them again and again. But you would not listen, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes the renewed direct address explicit.
verses.before: But hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.after: “But you, all the exiles whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon, hear the word of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: But hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fathers' names to distinguish these men from kings of the same names.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in my name: I am about to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says this about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who prophesy lies to you in my name: I will hand them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying a lie to you in my name: I am about to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains the brutal manner of killing and the order of names in the curse.

verses.after: All the exiles of Judah in Babylon will use their fate as a curse: ‘May the **LORD** make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And from them shall be taken up a curse used by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon, who shall say, "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,"

verses.rationale: Follows the read 'one who knows' despite the divided written form; preserves adultery and unauthorized speech.

verses.after: For they have done an outrage in Israel: they committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and spoke lies in my name that I did not command them to speak. I am the one who knows, and I am witness, declares the **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: because they committed outrage in Israel, committing adultery with their neighbors' wives and speaking in my name a lying word that I had not commanded them. I am the one who knows; I am a witness, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the new recipient's identifying designation without inventing its origin.
verses.before: To Shemaiah of Nehelam you will say:
verses.after: Tell Shemaiah the Nehelamite:

verses.rationale: Preserves the unauthorized sender's own name and all letter recipients while unpacking the long introductory syntax.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
verses.after: “The **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and to all the priests. You wrote:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have sent letters in your own name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps 'madman' within Shemaiah's hostile letter, and retains both devices of confinement with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: "The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be overseer in the house of the LORD over every madman who prophesies, that you may put him in the stocks and the collar.
verses.after: ‘The **LORD** has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, so that there will be officers in the house of the **LORD** to deal with every madman who acts as a prophet. You must put him in the stocks and the neck restraint.
verses.tsw_comparator: "The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be overseer in the house of the LORD over every madman who prophesies, that you may put him in the stocks and the collar.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hostile description and Jeremiah's hometown.
verses.before: Now then, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying among you?
verses.after: So why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who acts as a prophet among you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now then, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying among you?

verses.rationale: Retains the letter's quotation of Jeremiah and its repeated settlement commands.
verses.before: For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, 'It will be long. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.'"
verses.after: He has sent word to us in Babylon: “It will be a long time. Build houses and live in them. Plant gardens and eat their fruit.”’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has sent to us in Babylon, saying, 'It will be long. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.'"

verses.rationale: Keeps the priest's actual response distinct from the punishment Shemaiah requested.
verses.before: Now Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.after: Zephaniah the priest read this letter aloud to Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.

verses.rationale: Retains the revelation formula at the change of scene.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
verses.after: Then the word of the **LORD** came to Jeremiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

verses.rationale: Preserves the causal introduction and the two connected accusations.
verses.before: Send to all the exiles, saying, Thus says the LORD concerning Shemaiah of Nehelam: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you when I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,
verses.after: “Send this message to all the exiles: ‘The **LORD** says this about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah prophesied to you when I had not sent him, and made you trust a lie,

verses.rationale: Keeps the offspring consequence, exclusion from coming good, and all three divine-name occurrences.
verses.before: so thus says the LORD: I am about to punish Shemaiah of Nehelam and his offspring. He will not have anyone among this people to see the good that I am doing for my people, declares the LORD, for he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.
verses.after: the **LORD** says: I will call Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his offspring to account. He will have no one living among this people, and he will not see the good I am going to do for my people, declares the **LORD**, because he has preached rebellion against the **LORD**.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore thus says the LORD: I am about to punish Shemaiah of Nehelam and his offspring. He shall not have anyone among this people to see the good that I am doing for my people, declares the LORD, for he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the opening revelation formula.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,
verses.after: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD**:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the command for a written collection and its full scope.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Write for yourself in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.
verses.after: “The **LORD**, the God of Israel, says: Write in a scroll all the words I have spoken to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Write for yourself in a book all the words that I have spoken to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps both Israel and Judah, both speech formulas, and renewed possession of ancestral land.
verses.before: For look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah,” says the LORD. “I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their ancestors, and they will possess it.”
verses.after: For look, days are coming, declares the **LORD**, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the **LORD**. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will possess it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah,” says the LORD. “I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their ancestors, and they will possess it.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated identification of both peoples.
verses.before: These are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah:
verses.after: These are the words the **LORD** spoke concerning Israel and Judah:
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the words that the LORD spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah:

verses.rationale: Retains the first-person plural within the oracle rather than silently changing it to a narrator's report.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “A sound of trembling we have heard, terror and no peace.
verses.after: “The **LORD** says: We have heard a cry of terror, fear, and no peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “A sound of trembling we have heard, terror and no peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves the specifically male subjects and the childbirth comparison without neutralizing their contrast.
verses.before: Ask now and see: Can a male give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman giving birth, and every face turned pale?
verses.after: Ask and see: Can a male give birth? Why, then, do I see every man with his hands on his waist like a woman in labor? Why has every face turned pale?
verses.tsw_comparator: Ask now and see: Can a male give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman giving birth, and every face turned pale?

verses.rationale: Keeps the unparalleled distress and rescue from within it together.
verses.before: Alas! For that day is great; there is none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet from it he will be saved.
verses.after: Alas, that day is great; there is none like it! It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet he will be saved out of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Alas! For that day is great; there is none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet from it he will be saved.

verses.rationale: Preserves the source's shifts between second and third person and leaves the oppressor unnamed.
verses.before: “And it will be on that day,” says the LORD of Hosts, “I will break his yoke from your neck and tear off your bonds, and strangers will no longer make him serve.
verses.after: “On that day, declares the **LORD** of hosts, I will break his yoke from your neck and tear off your straps. Foreigners will no longer enslave him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will be on that day,” says the LORD of Hosts, “I will break his yoke from your neck and tear off your bonds, and strangers will no longer make him serve.

verses.rationale: Retains David as named rather than inserting a later identification or explaining away the wording.
verses.before: But they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
verses.after: They will serve the **LORD** their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names, the distant offspring, and the accumulated assurances of security.
verses.before: “And you, do not fear, Jacob my servant,” says the LORD, “and do not be dismayed, Israel. For look, I am saving you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and no one will make him afraid.
verses.after: So do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the **LORD**; do not be dismayed, Israel. I will save you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at rest, at ease, with no one to make him afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you, do not fear, Jacob my servant,” says the LORD, “and do not be dismayed, Israel. For look, I am saving you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and no one will make him afraid.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast in destruction while retaining real discipline and accountability.
verses.before: For I am with you,” says the LORD, “to save you. Though I make a complete end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, of you I will not make a complete end. I will discipline you in justice, but I will certainly not leave you unpunished.
verses.after: For I am with you to save you, declares the **LORD**. I will make an end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you with justice; I will certainly not leave you unpunished.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am with you,” says the LORD, “to save you. Though I make a complete end of all the nations among whom I scattered you, of you I will not make a complete end. I will discipline you in justice, but I will certainly not leave you unpunished.

verses.rationale: Retains both fracture and wound as bodily images of the people's condition.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “Your breaking is incurable; your wound is severe.
verses.after: “For the **LORD** says: Your fracture is beyond healing; your wound is grievous.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “Your breaking is incurable; your wound is severe.

verses.rationale: Keeps the legal and medical images alongside each other without collapsing them.
verses.before: There is no one to plead your case, no healing for your sore, no restoration for you.
verses.after: No one pleads your case. There is no treatment for your sore, no healing for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is no one to plead your case, no healing for your sore, no restoration for you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the speaker's direct agency, the lovers' abandonment, and the severity of the discipline.
verses.before: All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I struck you with the blow of an enemy, with the discipline of a cruel one, because your guilt was great and your sins were numerous.
verses.after: All your lovers have forgotten you; they no longer seek you out. I struck you as an enemy strikes, with cruel discipline, because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.
verses.tsw_comparator: All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I struck you with the blow of an enemy, with the discipline of a cruel one, because your guilt was great and your sins were numerous.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated accusation and the difficult attribution of suffering to the speaker.
verses.before: Why do you cry out over your breaking? Your pain is incurable. Because your guilt was great and your sins were numerous, I did these things to you.
verses.after: Why cry out over your fracture? Your pain is beyond healing. Because your guilt is so great and your sins so many, I have done these things to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you cry out over your breaking? Your pain is incurable. Because your guilt was great and your sins were numerous, I did these things to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves each reversal and the repeated totality of the enemies' captivity.
verses.before: “Therefore everyone who devour you will be devoured, and all your adversaries, every one of them, will go into captivity. People who plunder you will become plunder, and everyone who spoil you I will give as spoil.
verses.after: Yet all who devour you will be devoured; all your enemies, every one, will go into captivity. Those who plunder you will be plundered, and all who prey on you I will give up as prey.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore all who devour you will be devoured, and all your adversaries, every one of them, will go into captivity. Those who plunder you will become plunder, and all who spoil you I will give as spoil.

verses.rationale: Keeps the healing reversal and the contemptuous quotation about Zion.
verses.before: For I will bring healing to you and heal you of your wounds,” says the LORD, “because they called you an outcast: ‘This is Zion, for whom no one cares.’
verses.after: For I will restore your health and heal your wounds, declares the **LORD**, because they call you an outcast: ‘She is Zion; no one cares about her.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will bring healing to you and heal you of your wounds,” says the LORD, “because they called you an outcast: ‘This is Zion, for whom no one cares.’

verses.rationale: Retains tents, dwellings, city mound, and palace as distinct restoration images.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Look, I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt upon its mound, and the palace will stand in its proper place.
verses.after: “The **LORD** says: I will restore the fortunes of Jacob's tents and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt on its own mound, and the palace will stand in its rightful place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Look, I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt upon its mound, and the palace will stand in its proper place.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired reversals of dwindling numbers and diminished standing.
verses.before: Thanksgiving will come out from them, and the sound of people who rejoice. I will multiply them, and they will not become few; I will honor them, and they will not become small.
verses.after: Thanksgiving will come from them, and the sound of people celebrating. I will make them numerous; they will not dwindle. I will give them honor; they will not be insignificant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thanksgiving will come out from them, and the sound of those who rejoice. I will multiply them, and they will not become few; I will honor them, and they will not become small.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the antecedent Jacob and retains the restored community and punished oppressors.
verses.before: Their children will be as before, and their congregation will be established before me, and I will attend to everyone who oppress them.
verses.after: Jacob's children will be as they were before; his community will be established before me. I will call all his oppressors to account.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their children will be as before, and their congregation will be established before me, and I will attend to all who oppress them.

verses.rationale: Retains the native ruler and the difficult heart-pledging expression, explained briefly in a note.
verses.before: Their leader will be one of their own, and their ruler will come out from their midst. I will bring him near, and he will approach me, for who is this who has pledged his heart to approach me?” says the LORD.
verses.after: Their noble leader will be one of their own; their ruler will come from among them. I will bring him near, and he will approach me. For who would pledge his own heart to approach me? declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their leader will be one of their own, and their ruler will come out from their midst. I will bring him near, and he will approach me, for who is this who has pledged his heart to approach me?” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the clear covenant formula unchanged in substance.
verses.before: “And you will be my people, and I will be your God.”
verses.after: You will be my people, and I will be your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “And you will be my people, and I will be your God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the echo of 23:19 while distinguishing the storm's descriptive participle.
verses.before: Look, the storm of the LORD—wrath— has gone out, a sweeping storm; it will whirl upon the head of the wicked.
verses.after: Look! The storm of the **LORD**! Wrath has burst out, a sweeping storm; it whirls down on the heads of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the storm of the LORD—wrath— has gone out, a sweeping storm; it will whirl upon the head of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Maintains the deliberate echo of 23:20 without adding an end-times system.
verses.before: The burning anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and established the purposes of his heart. In the latter days you will understand this.
verses.after: The **LORD**'s burning anger will not turn back until he has done and accomplished what his heart intends. In days to come you will understand it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burning anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and established the purposes of his heart. In the latter days you will understand this.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inclusive all-clans wording and covenant relationship.
verses.before: “At that time,” says the LORD, “I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they will be my people.”
verses.after: “At that time, declares the **LORD**, I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they will be my people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “At that time,” says the LORD, “I will be God to all the clans of Israel, and they shall be my people.”

verses.rationale: Retains survivors, wilderness favor, and the difficult movement toward rest with alternate construal noted.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; when Israel sought rest,
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness, as Israel went to find rest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; when Israel sought rest,

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-person recipient and a spatial reading of distance while noting possible temporal and continuing-love senses.
verses.before: the LORD appeared to them from far away: ‘Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my steadfast love toward you.
verses.after: From far away the **LORD** appeared to me: “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with steadfast love.
verses.tsw_comparator: the LORD appeared to them from far away: ‘Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my steadfast love toward you.

verses.rationale: Preserves virgin Israel as a personification and the repeated 'again' of restored celebration.
verses.before: Again I will build you, and you will be built, O virgin Israel! Again you will take up your tambourines and go out in the dance of people who rejoice.
verses.after: I will build you again, and you will be rebuilt, virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out dancing with those who celebrate.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I will build you, and you shall be built, O virgin Israel! Again you shall take up your tambourines and go out in the dance of those who rejoice.

verses.rationale: Renders the technical release of produce into ordinary use as enjoyment, without omitting the planters' benefit.
verses.before: Again you will plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters will plant and will enjoy the fruit.
verses.after: Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria. Those who plant them will enjoy their fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant and shall enjoy the fruit.

verses.rationale: Retains Ephraim's movement toward Zion and the watchmen's direct invitation.
verses.before: For there will be a day when watchmen will call on the hills of Ephraim: ‘Rise up—let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.’”
verses.after: For a day is coming when watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim: ‘Come, let us go up to Zion, to the **LORD** our God!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For there shall be a day when watchmen will call on the hills of Ephraim: ‘Rise up—let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned imperative 'save' rather than changing it into an announcement that salvation has occurred.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “Sing aloud with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations; proclaim, give praise, and say, ‘O LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’
verses.after: For the **LORD** says: “Sing with joy for Jacob! Shout for the foremost of the nations! Make your praise heard and say, ‘**LORD**, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “Sing aloud with gladness for Jacob, and shout among the chief of the nations; proclaim, give praise, and say, ‘O LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel!’

verses.rationale: Keeps all specifically named vulnerable travelers and the large returning assembly.
verses.before: Look—I am bringing them from the land of the north, and gathering them from the farthest parts of the earth, among them the blind and the lame, the one who is pregnant and the one in labor together— a great company, they will return here.
verses.after: Look, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the farthest reaches of the earth. Among them will be the blind and those who are lame, pregnant women and women in labor together. A great assembly will return here.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look—I am bringing them from the land of the north, and gathering them from the farthest parts of the earth, among them the blind and the lame, the one who is pregnant and the one in labor together— a great company, they shall return here.

verses.rationale: Retains supplication rather than silently substituting consolation, and keeps water, safe path, and family images.
verses.before: With weeping they will come, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them back. I will cause them to walk by streams of water, on a level path in which they will not stumble, for I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
verses.after: They will come with weeping; with pleas for mercy I will lead them. I will guide them beside streams of water on a level path where they will not stumble. For I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
verses.tsw_comparator: With weeping they shall come, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them back. I will cause them to walk by streams of water, on a level path in which they shall not stumble, for I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.

verses.rationale: Preserves the same agent in scattering and gathering and the shepherd comparison.
verses.before: Hear the word of the LORD, O nations, and declare it in the coastlands far away: ‘The one who scattered Israel will gather Israel, and will keep watch over Israel like a shepherd over a flock.’
verses.after: Hear the word of the **LORD**, nations! Announce it on distant coastlands. Say, ‘The one who scattered Israel will gather him and guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the word of the LORD, O nations, and declare it in the coastlands far away: ‘The one who scattered Israel will gather Israel, and will keep watch over Israel like a shepherd over a flock.’

verses.rationale: Keeps both redemption verbs and the stronger hand image.
verses.before: For the LORD has redeemed Jacob and ransomed him from a hand stronger than his.
verses.after: For the **LORD** has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from a hand stronger than his.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD has redeemed Jacob and ransomed him from a hand stronger than his.

verses.rationale: Preserves the flowing movement, full produce list, and garden image of renewed life.
verses.before: They will come and sing aloud on the height of Zion, and they will be radiant over the goodness of the LORD— over the grain, the wine, and the oil, and over the young of the flock and the herd; their whole being will be like a watered garden, and they will languish no more.
verses.after: They will come and sing on Zion's height, streaming toward the goodness of the **LORD**— the grain, new wine, and oil, the young of the flocks and herds. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and they will languish no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall come and sing aloud on the height of Zion, and they shall be radiant over the goodness of the LORD— over the grain, the wine, and the oil, and over the young of the flock and the herd; their whole being shall be like a watered garden, and they shall languish no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps the age and gender groups and the doubled transformation of mourning.
verses.before: Then will the virgin rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, I will comfort them, and give them gladness for sorrow.
verses.after: Then young women will rejoice in dancing, and young men and old men together. I will turn their mourning into joy; I will comfort them and give them gladness in place of grief.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, I will comfort them, and give them gladness for sorrow.

verses.rationale: Retains material plenty and the paired satisfaction of priests and people.
verses.before: I will satisfy the priests with abundance, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will satisfy the priests with rich food, and my people will be filled with my goodness, declares the **LORD**.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will satisfy the priests with abundance, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Rachel's refusal and the repeated children, without prematurely resolving the lament into consolation.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lament and bitter weeping: Rachel weeps for her children. She refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the promised response after the lament and both divine declarations.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Keep your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for there is a reward for your work,” says the LORD, “and they will return from the land of the enemy.
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “Hold back your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your labor, declares the **LORD**. They will return from the enemy's land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Keep your voice from weeping, and your eyes from tears; for there is a reward for your work,” says the LORD, “and they shall return from the land of the enemy.

verses.rationale: Retains future hope as the children's return to their territory.
verses.before: There is hope for your future,” says the LORD, “and your children will return to their own border.
verses.after: There is hope for your future, declares the **LORD**; your children will return to their own territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is hope for your future,” says the LORD, “and your children shall return to their own border.

verses.rationale: Preserves the untrained-calf comparison and the causative/returning wordplay.
verses.before: I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: ‘You have disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.
verses.after: I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: ‘You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like a calf not yet trained. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the **LORD** my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: ‘You have disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily gesture and the sequence of return, understanding, and shame, with alternate turning sense noted.
verses.before: For after I turned away, I repented; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh; I was ashamed, and I was humiliated, for I bore the reproach of my youth.’
verses.after: After I turned back, I repented; after I came to understand, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed and humiliated, for I bore the disgrace of my youth.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For after I turned away, I repented; and after I was instructed, I struck my thigh; I was ashamed, and I was humiliated, for I bore the reproach of my youth.’

verses.rationale: Retains questions, persistent remembering, and visceral compassion rather than replacing the body image entirely with emotion.
verses.before: Is Ephraim my dear son? Is he my precious child? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my inner being yearns for him; I will surely have compassion on him,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Is Ephraim not a dear son to me, a child in whom I delight? Whenever I speak against him, I still remember him. That is why my inward parts stir for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is Ephraim my dear son? Is he my precious child? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my inner being yearns for him; I will surely have compassion on him,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows the read second-person feminine 'you went' and keeps the repeated return invitation.
verses.before: “Set up road markers for yourself; make yourself guideposts. Pay attention to the highway, the road by which you went. Return, O virgin Israel— return to these your cities!
verses.after: Set up road markers for yourself; put up signposts. Set your heart on the highway, the road by which you went. Return, virgin Israel; return to these towns of yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Set up road markers for yourself; make yourself guideposts. Pay attention to the highway, the road by which you went. Return, O virgin Israel— return to these your cities!

verses.rationale: Preserves the difficult woman/man image without imposing a courtship, military, or incarnation interpretation.
verses.before: How long will you wander, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman will encompass a man.”
verses.after: How long will you wander about, faithless daughter? For the **LORD** has created something new in the land: a woman will surround a man.”
verses.tsw_comparator: How long will you wander, O faithless daughter? For the LORD has created a new thing on the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the restored blessing and both names for the place addressed.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Once more they will say in the land of Judah and in its towns, when I restore their fortunes: ‘The LORD bless you, O habitation of righteousness, O holy mountain!’
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: “When I restore their fortunes, they will again say this in the land of Judah and its towns: ‘May the **LORD** bless you, dwelling of righteousness, holy mountain.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Once more they shall say in the land of Judah and in its towns, when I restore their fortunes: ‘The LORD bless you, O habitation of righteousness, O holy mountain!’

verses.rationale: Preserves the agricultural and mobile pastoral populations together.
verses.before: Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and people who wander with their flocks.
verses.after: Judah and all its towns will live there together—farmers and those who travel with the flocks.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Judah and all its towns shall live there together, the farmers and those who wander with their flocks.

verses.rationale: Retains the two kinds of need and their corresponding relief.
verses.before: For I will satisfy the weary soul, and every faint soul I will replenish.”
verses.after: For I will refresh every weary person and satisfy every person who languishes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will satisfy the weary soul, and every faint soul I will replenish.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the first-person waking report without assigning its speaker more explicitly than the text does.
verses.before: At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
verses.after: At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps both houses and the agricultural image applied to humans and animals.
verses.before: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of humans and the seed of animals.
verses.after: “Look, days are coming, declares the **LORD**, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of people and the seed of animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of humans and the seed of animals.

verses.rationale: Preserves every destructive verb and the repeated watching that now turns to restoration.
verses.before: And just as I have watched over them to pluck up and break down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Just as I watched over them to uproot, tear down, overthrow, destroy, and bring harm, so I will watch over them to build and plant, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as I have watched over them to pluck up and break down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the proverb's fathers, children, and bodily image.
verses.before: “In those days they will no longer say: ‘The parents have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’
verses.after: In those days they will no longer say, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “In those days they shall no longer say: ‘The parents have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge.’

verses.rationale: Preserves personal responsibility and the proverb's reapplied consequence.
verses.before: But each person will die for their own iniquity; everyone who eats sour grapes, their teeth will be set on edge.
verses.after: Instead, each person will die for their own guilt. Everyone who eats sour grapes will have their own teeth set on edge.
verses.tsw_comparator: But each one shall die for their own iniquity; everyone who eats sour grapes, their teeth shall be set on edge.

verses.rationale: Retains new covenant and both named recipients without replacing them with a later interpretive community.
verses.before: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will cut a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah—
verses.after: “Look, days are coming, declares the **LORD**, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will cut a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah—

verses.rationale: Preserves the hand-led exodus and the pinned marital/authority verb, with its range explained in a note.
verses.before: not like the covenant that I cut with their ancestors in the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt— my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband,” says the LORD.
verses.after: It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt. They broke my covenant, though I was their husband, declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: not like the covenant that I cut with their ancestors in the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt— my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps torah as instruction, the internal writing image, and the covenant formula.
verses.before: “For this is the covenant that I will cut with the house of Israel after those days,” says the LORD: “I will put my instruction within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be my people.
verses.after: This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the **LORD**: I will put my instruction within them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For this is the covenant that I will cut with the house of Israel after those days,” says the LORD: “I will put my instruction within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

verses.rationale: Preserves universal knowing within the named people and both forgiveness and no longer remembering.
verses.before: And they will no longer teach—each person their neighbor and each person their sister or brother—saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest,” says the LORD, “for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.”
verses.after: No longer will each person teach their neighbor or their brother, saying, ‘Know the **LORD**,’ for they will all know me, from the least to the greatest, declares the **LORD**. For I will forgive their guilt and remember their sin no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they shall no longer teach—each one their neighbor and each one their sister or brother—saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest,” says the LORD, “for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.”

verses.rationale: Retains the ordered lights and turbulent sea together in the speaker's identification.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD, who gives the sun for light by day, and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar— the LORD of Hosts is his name:
verses.after: The **LORD** says— the one who gives the sun for light by day, the fixed order of moon and stars for light by night, who stirs the sea so its waves roar, whose name is the **LORD** of hosts:

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional impossibility as the assurance of continued national existence.
verses.before: “If this fixed order departs from before me,” says the LORD, “then the offspring of Israel also will cease from being a nation before me forever.”
verses.after: “Only if this fixed order departs from before me, declares the **LORD**, will Israel's offspring cease to be a nation before me for all time.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “If this fixed order departs from before me,” says the LORD, “then the offspring of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me forever.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both cosmic conditions and the repeated 'all' of offspring and deeds.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will also reject all the offspring of Israel because of all that they have done,” says the LORD.
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “Only if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below explored will I reject all Israel's offspring because of all they have done,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below can be explored, then I will also reject all the offspring of Israel because of all that they have done,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Includes the read word 'coming' supplied in the margin and preserves both boundary landmarks.
verses.before: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
verses.after: “Look, days are coming, declares the **LORD**, when the city will be rebuilt for the **LORD**, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look—the days are coming,” says the LORD, “when the city shall be rebuilt for the LORD from the tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.

verses.rationale: Follows the read measuring-line form and retains both uncertain place names.
verses.before: The measuring line will go out farther straight ahead to the hill Gareb, and then turn to Goah.
verses.after: The measuring line will extend from there to the hill of Gareb and turn toward Goah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The measuring line shall go out farther straight ahead to the hill Gareb, and then turn to Goah.

verses.rationale: Follows the read fields form and preserves the disturbing valley description and complete boundary sequence.
verses.before: The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the Wadi Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will not be plucked up or overthrown any more forever.”
verses.after: The whole valley of corpses and ashes, and all the fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the **LORD**. It will never again be uprooted or demolished.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the fields as far as the Wadi Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, shall be holy to the LORD. It shall not be plucked up or overthrown any more forever.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both regnal dates and follows the read year form.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.after: This word came to Jeremiah from the **LORD** in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.

verses.rationale: Keeps siege and confinement simultaneous and identifies the courtyard setting.
verses.before: At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard that was in the house of the king of Judah.
verses.after: At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the guard courtyard of the palace of the king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard that was in the house of the king of Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king's accusation and its quotation of the oracle.
verses.before: For Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, “Why do you prophesy, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it;
verses.after: Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him, saying, “Why do you prophesy this: ‘The **LORD** says: I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it?

verses.rationale: Follows the read plural eyes and keeps both direct encounter expressions.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unspecified future attention and the warning that resistance will fail.

verses.before: Jeremiah said, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact kinship and the legal reason for purchase.
verses.before: ‘Look, Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying, “Buy for yourself my field that is at Anathoth, for the right of redemption to buy it belongs to you.”’
verses.after: ‘Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is coming to you. He will say, “Buy my field at Anathoth, because you have the right of redemption to buy it.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Look, Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying, “Buy for yourself my field that is at Anathoth, for the right of redemption to buy it belongs to you.”’

verses.rationale: Keeps both property rights and the recognition that follows the visit.
verses.before: Then Hanamel my cousin came to me in the court of the guard according to the word of the LORD and said to me, ‘Please buy my field that is at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for the right of inheritance is yours and the redemption is yours. Buy it for yourself.’ Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.

Buy it for yourself.’ Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Combines seven and ten into seventeen without changing the weight or introducing coins.
verses.before: So I bought the field at Anathoth from Hanamel my cousin and weighed out the silver to him: seventeen shekels of silver.
verses.after: “So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out the silver for him: seventeen shekels.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four formal actions and the weighed payment.

verses.tsw_comparator: I wrote the deed, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the silver on scales.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact year and royal genealogy.
verses.before: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the full geographical and temporal scope of the written collection.
verses.before: “Take for yourself a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel, concerning Judah, and concerning all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah until this day.
