verses.rationale: Preserves the possibility of hearing, turning, and forgiveness rather than presenting judgment as mechanically unavoidable.
verses.before: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the disaster that I intend to do to them, so that each may turn from his evil way, and I may forgive their guilt and their sin.”
verses.after: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear of all the disaster I intend to bring on them and turn back, each from their evil way. Then I can forgive their guilt and sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the disaster that I intend to do to them, so that each may turn from his evil way, and I may forgive their guilt and their sin.”

verses.rationale: Makes the mouth-to-writing process readable while preserving the source of the words.
verses.before: Then Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.
verses.after: Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah. As Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on a scroll all the words the **LORD** had spoken to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the nature of the restriction unspecified rather than asserting imprisonment here.
verses.before: Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, “I am restricted; I cannot enter the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Then Jeremiah instructed Baruch: “I am prevented from going to the house of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, “I am restricted; I cannot enter the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the fasting occasion, both divine names, and both local and visiting listeners.
verses.before: So you go and read from the scroll that you wrote from my mouth the words of the LORD in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD on a fast day. Also in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities you will read them.
verses.after: So you must go on a day of fasting and read aloud from the scroll the words of the **LORD** that you wrote at my dictation. Read them in the house of the **LORD** to the people, including all those who come from Judah's towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you go and read from the scroll that you wrote from my mouth the words of the LORD in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD on a fast day. Also in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities you shall read them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the falling-plea image and both divine names in the appeal.
verses.before: Perhaps their plea will fall before the LORD, and each will turn from his evil way, for great is the anger and fury that the LORD has spoken against this people.”
verses.after: Perhaps their plea for mercy will fall before the **LORD**, and each will turn back from their evil way. For great are the anger and wrath the **LORD** has announced against this people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Perhaps their plea will fall before the LORD, and each will turn from his evil way, for great is the anger and fury that the LORD has spoken against this people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the summary of obedience and the repeated name.
verses.before: Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.
verses.after: Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of the **LORD** in the house of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the later year, exact month, and both participating groups.
verses.before: In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the LORD.
verses.after: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, all the people in Jerusalem and all who had come from Judah's towns to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named room, upper courtyard, gate, and public audibility.
verses.before: Then Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
verses.after: Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll in the house of the **LORD**, in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard at the entrance to the New Gate of the house of the **LORD**. All the people could hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the listener's three-generation identity and all the words heard.
verses.before: When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll,
verses.after: Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the **LORD** read from the scroll.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Micaiah son of Gemariah, son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll,

verses.rationale: Keeps every named official and father, distinguishing this Zedekiah from the king.
verses.before: he went down to the king’s house, to the scribe’s chamber. Look, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
verses.after: He went down to the royal palace, to the scribe's room. All the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
verses.tsw_comparator: he went down to the king’s house, to the scribe’s chamber. Look, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.

verses.rationale: Retains the chain from public reading to reported words.
verses.before: Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.
verses.after: Micaiah told them everything he had heard Baruch read from the scroll to the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four-generation messenger identification and the requested physical scroll.
verses.before: Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people and come.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
verses.after: All the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch with this message: “Take the scroll you read to the people and come.” Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and went to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people and come.” So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the courteous request and its fulfillment.
verses.before: They said to him, “Please sit and read it in our hearing.” So Baruch read it in their hearing.
verses.after: They said, “Please sit down and read it to us.” So Baruch read it to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to him, “Please sit and read it in our hearing.” So Baruch read it in their hearing.

verses.rationale: Preserves their fear and emphatic decision to report everything.
verses.before: When they heard all the words, they turned in fear each toward his neighbor and said to Baruch, “We must surely tell the king all these words.”
verses.after: When they heard all the words, they looked at one another in fear and told Baruch, “We must report all these words to the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When they heard all the words, they turned in fear each toward his neighbor and said to Baruch, “We must surely tell the king all these words.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the question focused on the writing process and oral source.
verses.before: They asked Baruch, saying, “Please tell us, how did you write all these words from his mouth?”
verses.after: They asked Baruch, “Please tell us how you wrote all these words at his dictation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They asked Baruch, saying, “Please tell us, how did you write all these words from his mouth?”

verses.rationale: Preserves dictation, writing surface, and ink as distinct details.
verses.before: Baruch said to them, “He dictated all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them with ink on the scroll.”
verses.after: Baruch answered, “He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them on the scroll in ink.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Baruch said to them, “He dictated all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them with ink on the scroll.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both men in the protective instruction and the secrecy required.
verses.before: Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.”
verses.after: The officials told Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Do not let anyone know where you are.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the officials said to Baruch, “Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the stored scroll and oral report before the king orders the document fetched.
verses.before: They went to the king in the court, but deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they told all the words in the hearing of the king.
verses.after: They left the scroll in Elishama the scribe's room and went into the courtyard to the king. They reported all the words to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went to the king in the court, but deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they told all the words in the hearing of the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps the messenger, storage location, and expanded royal audience.
verses.before: Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. He took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the officials standing beside the king.
verses.after: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. He took it from Elishama the scribe's room and read it to the king and all the officials standing beside him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. He took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the officials standing beside the king.

verses.rationale: Retains the season marker, winter residence, and fire container.
verses.before: The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.
verses.after: It was the ninth month. The king was sitting in his winter quarters, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated cutting process, exact number range, and complete destruction; explicit king follows the narrative's attribution in 27–29.
verses.before: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them with the scribe’s knife and throw them into the fire that was in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.
verses.after: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut them off with a scribe's knife and threw them into the fire in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them with the scribe’s knife and throw them into the fire that was in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the brazier.

verses.rationale: Retains both absent reactions, contrasting the officials' earlier fear.
verses.before: The king and all his servants who heard all these words did not fear, nor did they tear their garments.
verses.after: Neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words became afraid or tore their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king and all his servants who heard all these words did not fear, nor did they tear their garments.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three dissenting officials rather than flattening the court into one response.
verses.before: Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he did not listen to them.
verses.after: Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he did not listen to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three arrest agents and the final divine protection.
verses.before: The king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the LORD hid them.
verses.after: The king ordered Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the **LORD** hid them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king commanded Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the LORD hid them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sequence and the repeated oral-to-written origin.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,
verses.after: After the king had burned the scroll containing the words Baruch wrote at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the **LORD** came to Jeremiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves replacement and the command to restore all earlier words.
verses.before: “Take for yourself another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
verses.after: “Take another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take for yourself another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king's stated objection and both human and animal losses predicted.
verses.before: And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you will say: Thus says the LORD: You burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why did you write on it, saying, “The king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and cause human and animal to cease from it”?’
verses.after: And say about Jehoiakim king of Judah: ‘The **LORD** says: You burned this scroll, saying, “Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon will certainly come, devastate this land, and leave it without people or animals?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say: Thus says the LORD: You burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why did you write on it, saying, “The king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and cause human and animal to cease from it”?’

verses.rationale: Retains the dynastic threat and the unburied body's contrasting exposures.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.
verses.after: So the **LORD** says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on David's throne. His body will be thrown out, exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body will be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

verses.rationale: Preserves each responsible group and the refusal to listen as the concluding reason.
verses.before: I will attend to him, his offspring, and his servants for their guilt. I will bring upon them and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the men of Judah all the disaster that I spoke against them, but they did not listen.”
verses.after: I will call him, his offspring, and his servants to account for their guilt. I will bring on them, on Jerusalem's inhabitants, and on the people of Judah all the disaster I announced to them, because they did not listen.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will attend to him, his offspring, and his servants for their guilt. I will bring upon them and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the men of Judah all the disaster that I spoke against them, but they did not listen.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both full replacement and additional words without claiming the second scroll was identical in scope.
verses.before: Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many words like them were added to them.
verses.after: Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe. At Jeremiah's dictation he wrote on it all the words of the scroll Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. Many more words like them were added.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many words like them were added to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the succession and Babylonian appointment.
verses.before: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.
verses.after: Zedekiah son of Josiah became king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made him king over the land of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three non-listening groups.
verses.before: But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.after: Neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words the **LORD** spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
verses.tsw_comparator: But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that he spoke by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

verses.rationale: Retains both envoys and their fathers, and the request for intercession.
verses.before: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Please pray to the LORD our God for us.”
verses.after: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to Jeremiah the prophet with this request: “Please pray to the **LORD** our God for us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “Please pray to the LORD our God for us.”

verses.rationale: Follows the read prison form and preserves the chronology before confinement.
verses.before: Now Jeremiah was coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
verses.after: Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people; they had not yet put him in prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Jeremiah was coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reported movement as the cause of the temporary withdrawal.
verses.before: Pharaoh’s army had come out from Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt. When the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem heard the news, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh’s army had come out from Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the revelation formula and prophet title.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
verses.after: Then the word of the **LORD** came to Jeremiah the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the stated purpose of Egyptian aid and its reversal.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Thus you will say to the king of Judah who sent you to me to inquire of me: Look, Pharaoh’s army that came out to help you will return to its own land, Egypt.
verses.after: “The **LORD**, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of me: Pharaoh's army, which marched out to help you, is going back to its own land, Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: Thus you shall say to the king of Judah who sent you to me to inquire of me: Look, Pharaoh’s army that came out to help you will return to its own land, Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full sequence of promised military actions.
verses.before: Then the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it with fire.
verses.after: The Chaldeans will return, fight this city, capture it, and burn it down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic false assurance and its direct denial.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, ‘The Chaldeans will surely go away from us,’ for they will not go away.
verses.after: The **LORD** says: Do not deceive yourselves by saying, ‘The Chaldeans will surely leave us.’ They will not leave.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, ‘The Chaldeans will surely go away from us,’ for they will not go away.

verses.rationale: Retains the extreme hypothetical and the wounded survivors' action without making it a historical report.
verses.before: For even if you struck the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you and only wounded men remained among them, each man would rise in his tent and burn this city with fire.”
verses.after: Even if you defeated the whole Chaldean army fighting against you, leaving only wounded men, each would rise from his tent and burn this city down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For even if you struck the entire army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you and only wounded men remained among them, each man would rise in his tent and burn this city with fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the timing clause open for Jeremiah's attempted departure.
verses.before: When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s army,
verses.after: When the Chaldean army withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
verses.tsw_comparator: When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh’s army,

verses.rationale: Uses the allotment sense of the difficult verb and notes uncertainty about the precise errand.
verses.before: Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to receive his portion there among the people.
verses.after: Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem for the land of Benjamin to receive his share there among the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah went out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to receive his portion there among the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the officer's three-generation identity and accusation as speech.

verses.after: At the Benjamin Gate, a guard officer named Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, seized Jeremiah the prophet. “You are deserting to the Chaldeans!” he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he was at the Benjamin Gate, an officer of the guard was there whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. He seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “You are falling away to the Chaldeans!”

verses.rationale: Keeps Jeremiah's denial and the official's refusal to hear it.

verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah said, “False! I am not falling away to the Chaldeans.” But he did not listen to him. So Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.

verses.rationale: Preserves the officials' direct beating and the converted-house prison.
verses.before: The officials were angry with Jeremiah, struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into a prison.
verses.after: The officials were angry with Jeremiah. They beat him and imprisoned him in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had made into a prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: The officials were angry with Jeremiah, struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made it into a prison.

verses.rationale: Retains both confinement terms and duration, with the rare cell term noted.
verses.before: Jeremiah entered the dungeon house and the cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.
verses.after: Jeremiah was put into the dungeon, into its cells, and remained there many days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah entered the dungeon house and the cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the secret setting and blunt reply without softening its content.
verses.before: Then King Zedekiah sent and took him out. The king asked him secretly in his house and said, “Is there a word from the LORD?” Jeremiah said, “There is.” Then he said, “You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.”
verses.after: Then King Zedekiah sent for him. In his palace the king secretly asked, “Is there a word from the **LORD**?” Jeremiah answered, “There is. You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Zedekiah sent and took him out. The king asked him secretly in his house and said, “Is there a word from the LORD?” Jeremiah said, “There is.” Then he said, “You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon.”

verses.rationale: Retains the challenge to the three groups involved.
verses.before: Jeremiah also said to King Zedekiah, “How have I sinned against you, or against your servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
verses.after: Jeremiah also said to King Zedekiah, “What wrong have I done to you, your servants, or this people, that you have put me in prison?

verses.tsw_comparator: But I will deliver you on that day,” says the LORD, “and you will not be given into the hand of the men whom you fear.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic rescue, life as plunder, and trust as the stated reason.
verses.before: For I will surely rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword. Your life will be to you as plunder, because you trusted in me,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will certainly deliver you. You will not fall by the sword; your own life will be your plunder, because you trusted in me, declares the **LORD**.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will surely rescue you, and you will not fall by the sword. Your life will be to you as plunder, because you trusted in me,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the new heading and chains at Ramah without inventing a harmonizing account of how he arrived there after chapter 39.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had sent him from Ramah, when he took him bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.
verses.after: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD** after Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, released him at Ramah. He had taken Jeremiah while he was bound in chains among all the exiles from Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had sent him from Ramah, when he took him bound in chains among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried into exile to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the Babylonian officer as speaker of the theological explanation.
verses.before: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, “The LORD your God spoke this disaster against this place.
verses.after: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said, “The **LORD** your God announced this disaster against this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, “The LORD your God spoke this disaster against this place.

verses.rationale: Makes the plural accusation explicit so Jeremiah is not mistaken for its sole object; preserves both divine names.
verses.before: And the LORD has brought it and done just as he spoke, because you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice. Therefore this thing has come upon you.
verses.after: The **LORD** has brought it about and done just as he said. Because you people sinned against the **LORD** and did not listen to his voice, this has happened to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD has brought it and done just as he spoke, because you sinned against the LORD and did not listen to his voice. Therefore this thing has come upon you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two offered choices and the release from physical bonds.
verses.before: And now, look, I release you today from the chains that are on your hands. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes upon you. But if it is evil in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, refrain. See, the whole land is before you. Wherever it is good and right in your eyes to go, go there.”
verses.after: Now, today, I am freeing you from the chains on your hands. If you would like to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. If you do not want to come with me to Babylon, stay. The whole land lies before you. Go wherever seems good and right to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, look, I release you today from the chains that are on your hands. If it is good in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes upon you. But if it is evil in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, refrain. See, the whole land is before you. Wherever it is good and right in your eyes to go, go there.”

verses.rationale: Gives a restrained reading of the difficult opening clause and preserves the renewed choice and provisions.
verses.before: While Jeremiah had not yet turned away, Nebuzaradan said, “Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and live with him among the people. Or go wherever it is right in your eyes to go.” Then the captain of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and sent him away.
verses.after: Before Jeremiah turned to go, the captain added, “Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over Judah's towns. Live with him among the people, or go wherever you think best.” The captain of the guard gave him food and a gift and sent him away.
verses.tsw_comparator: While Jeremiah had not yet turned away, Nebuzaradan said, “Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and live with him among the people. Or go wherever it is right in your eyes to go.” Then the captain of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and sent him away.

verses.rationale: Keeps the chosen destination and remaining community.
verses.before: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.
verses.after: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people left in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the commanders outside the city and all groups entrusted to the governor.
verses.before: When all the commanders of the armies who were in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had entrusted to him men, women, little children, and some of the poor of the land who had not been carried into exile to Babylon,
verses.after: All the army commanders in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and put him in charge of the men, women, children, and poorest people who had not been exiled to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the commanders of the armies who were in the field, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land and had entrusted to him men, women, little children, and some of the poor of the land who had not been carried into exile to Babylon,

verses.rationale: Follows the read Ephai and preserves all names, brothers, and geographical identifiers.
verses.before: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.after: They came with their men to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite.
verses.tsw_comparator: they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath and conditions of remaining under foreign rule.
verses.before: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, saying, “Do not fear serving the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.
verses.after: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, saying, “Do not fear serving the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.

verses.rationale: Makes standing before the authorities readable while retaining all three harvest products and storage.
verses.before: As for me, look, I will live at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, put them in your vessels, and live in your cities that you have taken.”
verses.after: I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. You should gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, store them in your containers, and live in the towns you have taken over.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As for me, look, I will live at Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather wine, summer fruit, and oil, put them in your vessels, and live in your cities that you have taken.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct neighboring locations and the report prompting return.
verses.before: Likewise, when all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the children of Ammon, in Edom, and in all the lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan,
verses.after: All the Judeans in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands also heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Likewise, when all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the children of Ammon, in Edom, and in all the lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan,

verses.rationale: Preserves return, destination, and the two products actually named here.
verses.before: then all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They gathered wine and summer fruit in very great abundance.
verses.after: So all these Judeans returned from every place where they had been scattered. They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah in the land of Judah and gathered a great abundance of wine and summer fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: then all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been driven and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They gathered wine and summer fruit in very great abundance.

verses.after: They said, “Do you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to kill you?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to him, “Do you know that Baalis king of the children of Ammon has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to strike your life?” But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the proposed secret killing and its claimed preventive purpose without endorsing it.
verses.before: Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, “Please let me go and strike Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike your life, so that all the Judeans gathered to you are scattered and the remnant of Judah perishes?”
verses.after: Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah: “Please let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah. No one will know. Why should he kill you, scatter all the Judeans gathered around you, and destroy what remains of Judah?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, saying, “Please let me go and strike Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he strike your life, so that all the Judeans gathered to you are scattered and the remnant of Judah perishes?”

verses.rationale: Follows the read prohibition and keeps the denial as Gedaliah's judgment.

verses.after: Gedaliah son of Ahikam told Johanan son of Kareah, “Do not do this. What you are saying about Ishmael is a lie.”
